Auto-answered by the orchestrator clarify-respond workflow.

DECISIONS:
Q1: A
Q2: B

RATIONALE:
Q1: Target the default branch `main`. According to GitHub, PR #6576 (`ai/issue-6573` at `58ac3922e434`) is still open and unmerged, and the triage says it does not change `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py` or `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`. So a failing poller test is most likely also failing on `main`, and fixing it there unblocks every PR, #6576 included. The implementer works from its own checkout and its sandbox has no network access, so it cannot fetch the PR head. That rules out option C, and option B has no evidence behind it.
Q2: A bounded set of repeat runs is cheap. The selected group runs in about 5 minutes on 4 workers (`.github/workflows/ci.yml` comment, lines 1278-1281), well inside the 60-minute budget. Repeats are the only way to catch an intermittent failure without guessing at a cause. If no run fails, it behaves like A: no code change. Option C's speculative hardening is out of scope.

EXECUTION PLAN (required for any non-letter decision):
Q1:
  strategy: derive_from_repo
  inputs:
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml lines 1304-1333 (test list: top-level `test_*` functions in tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py, sorted, minus `test_implementation_failed_*`)
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml lines 1390-1398 (group `NR % 4 == 3`, then shard `NR % 4 == 1` within the group; job-index 3 of job-total 4, CI_POLL_TEST_SHARDS=4)
  steps:
    - Rebuild /tmp/orchestrate_poll_remaining_tests.txt on the `main` checkout using the same AST snippet as ci.yml lines 1307-1333.
    - Select group 3 with `awk -v n=3 -v total=4 'NR % total == n'`. Run every test in that group, not only shard 1, because `main` may have a different test list from PR head 58ac3922 and so a different shard boundary. Use `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py <names...>`.
    - Look for `FAIL` / `TEST_CASE_EVENT ... status=fail` lines. If a test fails, fix the root cause in its assertion or fixture. Change `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` only if the failing test shows a real poller defect. Do not change the aggregate `lint` gate or the sharding logic.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: "rerun that named test at this PR head" becomes "run the CI group-3 test set on `main`"
  equivalence_argument: The PR does not change the module under test, so `main` runs the same test code. Running the whole group covers shard 1 even if the shard boundaries moved.
  reversibility: If a person later shows the failure exists only on the PR branch, the fix can be cherry-picked or the PR rebased. A test-only fix on `main` is safe to revert.

Q2:
  strategy: reframe
  inputs:
    - The group-3 test list from Q1
  steps:
    - If the first run of group 3 passes, run the same list 2 more times, 3 runs at most. Run once with 4 parallel shards, as CI does, because parallel load is the likely timing difference.
    - If any run fails, fix that test, or the poller if the test shows a real defect. Then rerun the failing test until it passes 3 times in a row.
    - If all 3 runs pass, make no code change. The final summary lists the tests run and says the failure did not reproduce in 3 runs. The existing no-op handling then closes the issue, which is the same outcome as A.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: "fix only if the failure reproduces" becomes "fix only if any of up to 3 runs fails"
  equivalence_argument: This keeps the triage rule of no speculative changes, and still gives an intermittent failure a bounded chance to show up.
  reversibility: Nothing changes unless a run fails, so there is nothing to undo.
